Note regarding the `new-api-needs-documentation` label:

This serves as a reminder for when your PR is modifying a ref *.cs file and adding/modifying public APIs, to please make sure the API implementation in the src *.cs file is documented with triple slash comments, so the PR reviewers can sign off that change.

I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this PR. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-runtime See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Closes #1534 This PR adds the following API: ```csharp namespace System { public static partial class Nullable { public static ref readonly T GetValueRefOrDefaultRef(in T? nullable) where T : struct; } } ```
Author: Sergio0694
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Runtime`, `new-api-needs-documentation`
Milestone: -

Note: ideally the unit tests would compare the actual address, but they can't directly access internals from corelib and I'm not sure what the recommended approach is for this other than using a dynamic method, which seems a bit overkill and also potentially problematic for eg. NativeAOT? I'd have loved to use the APIs from #23716 if they had been implemented already 😄

Let me know if the included tests are enough or if any changes are recommended in that area 👍

Thank you @stephentoub and @tannergooding for helping push this through! 😄
I'll be adding a .NET 7 target to the HighPerformance package soon to leverage this too 😋

issue_context.title: API proposal: Nullable.RefValue, RefValueOrDefault

review_comments: Is there anywhere in dotnet/runtime we should be using this?

Mmh most examples I could find were with small primitive values (eg. `int`, `long` and whatnot). I've found this which might potentiall be a good candidate (given that `ValueTask<T>` is large enough), but then again this is within an asynchronous method so it wouldn't work without restructuring those few lines a bit more, which I'm not sure is necessarily worth it:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a5fda753afce966b9d31c76559636eb515bfa05a/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/HttpConnection.cs#L558-L572

Otherwise I'm not really finding that many examples, at least for now 🤔
Ok, thanks.  Sounds like we'll start using it in the DllImportGenerator, but we can leave that for later.

Can you add a test variant of this that does the same thing, except with a null T?, validating that after writing unsafely to the value, Value still throws an exception and HasValue is still false, but that you can still read the value out via the ref readonly?
